transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Rogers (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maria Thompson (SagePharm Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (InfoSec), Ethan Park (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick POC scoping to determine whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense for SagePharm's 3 pilot workloads. Focus on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timeline.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jamie): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro 

- Jamie Rogers, AE at Redwood, with Samir our SE and Alex our CSM. Maria, want to kick off with a little context on what you're trying to validate in the POC?
00:18 Dr. Maria: Yeah thanks Jamie. we're building a clinical document ingestion pipeline. three main workloads: 1) entity extraction and de-identification, 2) long-form summarization for clinicians, and 3) embedding/indexing for semantic search. goal for the POC is to validate latency and cost at scale and confirm security controls - particularly data residency and KMS integration.
00:40 Samir (Redwood SE): Great, that's helpful. quick high-level question: are you leaning toward a hosted SaaS first, or do you already have strict requirements that push to Dedicated or Private?
00:52 Dr. Maria: Ideally hosted for speed, but InfoSec might push us to Dedicated or Private because of PHI. Priya, do you want to outline the main restrictions?
01:03 Priya (InfoSec): Sure. Primary is data residency - records must remain in our VPC or an approved cloud region. Also need customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), audit logs for every inference call, and SOC2 plus ISO27001 evidence. We also have a procurement timeline; vendor security review takes 6-8 weeks.
01:24 Jamie: Ok got it. Redwood has options: Hosted API for fastest onboarding; Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and isolation; Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for strict compliance. We can support customer-managed KMS and provide audit logs. The tradeoff is time-to-launch and cost.
01:40 Liam (Cloud Architect): For sizing, we average about 200k new tokens/day now across internal tests, but peak concurrency matters - at times we could have 30 concurrent sessions doing long summaries (~3-4k tokens each). embeddings are batched, roughly 50k vectors/week. Latency requirements: summaries should be sub 3s p95 ideally, extraction can tolerate up to 5s p95.
02:05 Samir: OK that's useful. For the POC we'll want your sample prompt set and a traffic profile (p50/p95 token sizes, concurrency). We'll run benchmarks against our hosted runtime first to measure p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens. If we hit latency issues, we'll evaluate Dedicated with GPU pool and model/quantization tradeoffs.
02:22 Ethan (PM): timeline wise procurement can greenlight a pilot by mid-Feb if vendor docs are clean. Ideally pilot start week of Feb 10.
02:30 Speaker 2 (Alex CSM): We'll aim for a 2-3 week pilot with 2 baseline success criteria: 1) p95 latency under target for each workload, 2) unit cost within your budget envelope. Anything else?
02:45 Dr. Maria: Also accuracy/regression - we need to ensure no quality drop vs our baseline models. we'll provide evaluation prompts.
03:00 Samir: Good call. we'll run both perf and quality checks; our Redwood Optimize recommendations will include batching, prefix caching and quantization options. note: prefix caching may help with your repeated clinical templates.
03:20 Priya: For dedicated or private, does Redwood support air-gapped on-prem? We have some datasets that cannot leave premises.
03:28 Jamie: Yes, Redwood Private offers on-prem packages; that path has the longest lead time (typically 6-10 weeks for deployment and security verification) and higher fixed platform fees. Dedicated (reserved capacity) sits in the middle - faster than private, slower than hosted, but gives you predictable throughput and stronger isolation.
03:50 Liam: cost wise, can you ballpark delta between hosted vs dedicated? we need to present to finance.
03:56 Samir: ballpark: hosted is pay-as-you-go - lower upfront but higher per-token at scale; dedicated is a reserved commit with lower per-token when you utilize the capacity. private has the highest fixed cost but maximum control. We'll send a pricing template. For the POC we'll model 1M tokens/day as a scenario.
04:20 Speaker 3 (Maria): For benchmarks, what exactly will Redwood run?
04:25 Samir: We'll set up three benchmark suites: entity extraction (short prompts, high QPS), summarization (long sequences, high token output), embeddings (batched throughput). We'll measure p50/p95 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), memory/KV cache behaviour, and cost per 1M tokens using your token mix. We'll also run a small scale test on Dedicated variant to compare latency improvements and cost curves.
04:52 Priya: Will you provide SOC2 and data flow diagrams for our security review?
04:56 Alex: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation and network diagrams. For Private we can provide on-prem network runbook and KMS integration docs.
05:08 Ethan: On success criteria - beyond latency and cost - we need: audit logs retained for 12 months, SSO (SAML) integration, role-based access control, and exportability of logs to our SIEM.
05:22 Jamie: Redwood Console supports audit logs, tracing hooks and per-route dashboards; we can forward logs to your SIEM via TLS or S3. SAML SSO and RBAC are available on enterprise tiers.
05:36 Dr. Maria: Any model recommendations? we prefer open models due to licensing.
05:40 Samir: We'll propose a few open LLMs with quantization profiles - and also Redwood-verified performance profiles. For heavy summarization we might use an Llama-family optimized quantized variant; for extraction we can use smaller, faster models. We'll pin model versions for the POC so results are reproducible.
06:05 Speaker 6 (Customer): small Q - how do fallbacks work if capacity is saturated?
06:10 Samir: We do smart routing by policy; requests can fall back to compatible model variants or different regions. For Dedicated customers we can configure burst policies.
06:20 Dr. Maria: procurement wants to understand worst-case latency during peaks - can you simulate bursts?
06:25 Samir: yes, benchmark plan will include burst scenarios and tail latency under different batching configs.
06:34 Jamie: next up let's talk pilot success criteria and exit conditions - is the buy decision based on meeting p95 lat + cost targets and security signoff?
06:45 Dr. Maria: Exactly. If we meet the latency targets in hosted mode without breaking compliance, we prefer hosted. If not, Dedicated or Private are options - decision tree: hosted if p95 < target and SOC2+KMS can be satisfied; otherwise Dedicated if latency improves with reserved GPUs and security is OK; Private only if data cannot leave premises.
07:05 Priya: add on: Private required if PHI cannot be sent to any third party cloud region, otherwise Dedicated with VPC peering may suffice.
07:16 Liam: on sizing for Dedicated, what inputs do you need to propose a committed pool?
07:21 Samir: We'll need peak concurrent reqs, avg tokens per request, expected tokens/day, and target p95. Also preferred model family and sequence length distribution. With that we can propose GPU count, memory and autoscale policy.
07:40 Dr. Maria: We can provide a 7 day traffic dump and sample docs by Friday.
07:45 Alex: Great. we'll plan the pilot: week 1 setup + security review, week 2 benchmarks, week 3 eval + recommendations. That aligns with a mid-Feb start if procurement moves fast.
07:58 Ethan: who will be the technical owners?
08:02 Dr. Maria: Liam and Priya.
08:05 Alex: we'll add the Redwood SE and your cloud team to the pilot Slack channel.
08:10 Speaker 1 (Jamie): Ok let's capture next steps - Samir, you'll draft the benchmark plan; Alex will share pricing and SOC2 docs; Maria to send prompts and traffic. we aim to kick off week of Feb 10.
08:26 Dr. Maria: sounds good. thank you.
